# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. Path & Connection Puzzles
Games involving drawing or identifying connected paths

### A. Continuous Loop Puzzles
- Dotchi-Loop
- Hashiwokakero
- Masyu
- Mid-loop
- Slitherlink

### B. Path Tracing & Routing
- Hebi
- Nagareru
- Numberlink
- Sashigane
- Suraromu

## II. Polyomino & Tiling Puzzles
Games based on fitting or identifying polyominoes

### A. Free Polyomino Placement
- Evolomino
- LITS
- Shikaku

### B. Specific Polyomino Types
- Chained Block
- Fillomino
- Five Cells

### C. Domino & Tile Puzzles
- Choco Banana
- Double Choco
- Sto-stone
- Tilepaint

## III. Region & Area Division Puzzles
Games involving dividing grids into regions

### A. Pattern Recognition Regions
- Heyawake
- Norinori
- Ripple Effect
- Yosenabe

### B. Logic-Based Region Division
- Satogaeri
- Shakashaka

## IV. Shading & Coloring Puzzles
Games involving marking/shading cells with specific logic rules

### A. Simple Shading Logic
- Akari (inverse: placing light sources)
- Hitori
- Kurodoko
- Kurotto
- Nurikabe
- Nurimisaki
- Nuritwin

### B. Advanced Shading Patterns
- Makaro
- Moon-or-Sun
- Nurimeizu
- Usowan
- Yajilin

## V. Constraint & Clue-Based Puzzles
Games where numbers/clues determine cell contents

### A. Sudoku Variants
- Sudoku

### B. Clue-Based Deduction
- Juosan
- Nansuke
- Pencils

## VI. Hybrid Puzzles
Games combining multiple puzzle mechanics

- (Some games span multiple categories; detailed analysis recommends cross-referencing above sections)

---

**Note:** Some games could reasonably fit multiple categories. This taxonomy prioritizes the primary mechanic or most distinctive characteristic of each puzzle.
